title: Rethinking the Design Space of Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models: On the Importance of Likelihood Estimation Beyond Loss Design
claim: Our method reaches top benchmark score far faster than baselines, and the likelihood estimator, not the loss, drives the gain.
layout: 2 panels: large training-curve plot left, vertical 3-box flow right with key-findings text
description: The left panel is a large line plot of GenEval score against training time in GPU hours. A broken y-axis shows a lower segment near 0.2. Six series appear: a dashed gray baseline, FlowGRPO with CFG in teal, DiffusionNFT in gray, and three 'Ours' variants in blue, purple and red. Final scores are labeled at the line ends. The red ELBO-ODE curve rises steeply and plateaus at 0.97 within about 150 hours. The blue trajectory-SDE curve is noisy and slow. Dashed horizontal lines mark SD3.5-M at 0.63 and SD3.5-M without CFG at 0.24. The right panel stacks three rounded boxes joined by thick downward arrows: Policy-Gradient Loss Design, an orange-highlighted Likelihood Estimation (Trajectory vs. ELBO), and Sampling Strategy (SDE / ODE). Below them is an italic key-findings note. The eye goes first to the steep red curve, then to the orange box.
caption: Training efficiency and design-space analysis for reward-based diffusion fine-tuning. (Left) GenEval performance across training time for various fine-tuning methods on SD3.5-Medium. (Right) Conceptual summary of the design space considered in this work, highlighting policy-gradient loss design, likelihood estimation, and sampling strategy.
abstract: Reinforcement learning has been widely applied to diffusion and flow models for visual tasks such as text-to-image generation. However, these tasks remain challenging because diffusion models have intractable likelihoods, which creates a barrier for directly applying popular policy-gradient type methods. Existing approaches primarily focus on crafting new objectives built on already heavily engineered LLM objectives, using ad hoc estimators for likelihood, without a thorough investigation into how such estimation affects overall algorithmic performance. In this work, we provide a systematic analysis of the RL design space by disentangling three factors: i) policy-gradient objectives, ii) likelihood estimators, and iii) rollout sampling schemes. We show that adopting an evidence lower bound (ELBO) based model likelihood estimator, computed only from the final generated sample, is the dominant factor enabling effective, efficient, and stable RL optimization, outweighing the impact of the specific policy-gradient loss functional. We validate our findings across multiple reward benchmarks using SD 3.5 Medium, and observe consistent trends across all tasks. Our method improves the GenEval score from 0.24 to 0.95 in 90 GPU hours, which is 4.6 times more efficient than FlowGRPO and $2\times$ more efficient than the SOTA method without reward hacking.
